regions.model_reason: Retain the motor-lane classification. The satellite shows a paved pocket immediately left of the inbound rail corridor, bounded by longitudinal paint and occupied by vehicles. Its separate upstream extent is not established in the street views.
regions.model_binding: The requested crop resolves a left-bending directional arrow inside r1, between the dashed boundary on its left and the rail corridor on its right. Left-only is a lane-use prediction from this single-direction marking, not confirmed legal exclusivity: no applicable ONLY marking is readable. The mid-view camera cross-section does not securely show this additional pocket.

initial_surface_audit.evidence: Paired embedded rails run along paved roadway and continue into the intersection. Vehicles are aligned within the same track-bearing strip, supporting shared physical use rather than a separated rail reservation.

regions.model_reason: Retain shared rail/motor pavement. Satellite vehicles occupy the embedded-rail corridor. The mid street view shows embedded rails on paved roadway separated from the camera lane by broken white markings, rather than a physically segregated reservation.
regions.model_binding: The inbound rail pair immediately left of the mid-view camera corridor matches r2 through the rail–motor lane–green strip–curb ordering. Rail continuation does not establish motor turn permissions. Failure to identify rails in the older views does not demonstrate a spatial transition.

initial_surface_audit.evidence: Continuous asphalt strip between the track-bearing lane and narrow green strip. Longitudinal lane paint and aligned vehicles support a separate motor travel lane.

regions.model_reason: Retain motor lane. Satellite and mid street view both show a full-width motor corridor between the inbound rails and the narrow green strip.
regions.model_binding: The mid-view camera and utility truck lie between rails on the left and green pavement on the right, binding this corridor to r3. No readable lane-specific directional marking establishes through-only or shared movements.

initial_surface_audit.evidence: Narrow green-painted strip with longitudinal white boundaries continues toward the intersection between wider asphalt strips. The visible treatment and approximately 1.37 m width support bicycle-strip classification; no readable bicycle symbol is asserted.

regions.model_reason: Retain bicycle strip. The satellite crop confirms narrow green pavement inside the curbside motor corridor. The mid view preserves this ordering, while the older far view shows a narrow white-bordered strip with a faint bicycle marking.
regions.model_binding: Bound by r3 on its left and the curbside asphalt corridor on its right. The requested crop does not resolve a bicycle crossing or terminal movement marking. The older bicycle facility cannot establish unchanged stopbar continuity.

initial_surface_audit.evidence: Asphalt extends from the green strip to the physical curb and continues toward the intersection, with a vehicle near its upper end. Pale sidewalk paving lies beyond the curb. This supports a curbside motor travel lane, although its hinted width is relatively narrow and its exact movement function is not established. No parking stalls are discernible.

regions.model_reason: Retain motor lane, not parking or bicycle space. The satellite crop shows car-width asphalt running between the green strip and physical curb, with sidewalk beyond. Mid and far street views show the corresponding outer paved corridor. A stopped vehicle alone does not establish parking, and no parking stalls are identifiable within this region.
regions.model_binding: The green strip on the left and sidewalk curb on the right bind the crop to r5. A right-turn function is geometrically plausible, but the crop supplies no readable directional arrow or applicable restriction. A vehicle obscures the upper portion, and shadow crosses the exposed pavement. The curbside parking-restriction sign does not establish movement use.

initial_surface_audit.evidence: Continuous asphalt strip between the yellow center-side marking and a white longitudinal boundary. A vehicle occupies this strip immediately before the intersection markings. Vehicle and pole shadows obscure some pavement.

regions.model_reason: Retain the motor-lane classification. Satellite shows vehicle-occupied pavement immediately inside the yellow directional separator. Mid and far street views support an incoming motor lane on that side of the double yellow line.
regions.model_binding: The centerline-side position provides a provisional satellite-to-GSV correspondence. The requested near-view crop exposes only disconnected white marking fragments beside a vehicle; neither a complete directional arrow nor applicable ONLY text is resolved.

initial_surface_audit.evidence: This is paved, but appears to be a separator rather than a travel lane: continuous white boundaries flank it, and a triangular diagonal marking is visible along its continuation below the proposed region. The marking is not interpreted as a travel arrow. Resolution and shadows limit certainty about the complete buffer treatment.

regions.model_reason: The painted-buffer interpretation remains plausible but is not securely established. The native satellite crop shows two longitudinal boundaries and a pale triangular feature attached to one boundary, without resolving a complete separator treatment. GSV queues and framing prevent an independent identification of this exact strip.
regions.model_binding: This is the satellite strip between r1 and r3. The crop does not establish that its triangular feature is a lane-use arrow, but it also does not justify treating the preliminary buffer classification as certain. No GSV motor lane can be confidently bound to this polygon.

initial_surface_audit.evidence: Continuous roadway pavement lies between the solid separator-side boundary and a broken white lane divider. It continues toward the transverse intersection markings. A pole shadow covers part of its lower section.

regions.model_reason: Retain the motor-lane interpretation. Satellite shows a continuous car-width paved corridor between r2 and a broken white divider. GSV supports a multilane incoming roadway, although it does not independently expose this polygon's boundaries.
regions.model_binding: Bound principally by satellite ordering: immediately outside r2 and inside the vehicle-occupied r4 strip. Neither the crops nor the farther views provide a readable movement marking applicable to r3. Straight alignment is not evidence of through-only permission.

initial_surface_audit.evidence: Two clearly visible vehicles align within continuous roadway pavement bounded by longitudinal lane markings. The pavement continues to the intersection; vehicles obscure portions of its surface.

regions.model_reason: Retain the motor-lane interpretation. Satellite vehicles occupy a marked paved strip inward of the curbside region. The street views show incoming traffic queues rather than evidence that this roadway is exclusively parking.
regions.model_binding: Satellite lane-divider and curb ordering identify r4 between r3 and r5. Individual GSV queues cannot be securely matched to this polygon. No readable arrow or applicable lane-use sign establishes its movements.

initial_surface_audit.evidence: A car-width asphalt strip extends from the outer lane divider to the real curb. The sidewalk, pavers and planting lie outside that curb. No bicycle symbol, green treatment, parking stalls or parked vehicles are discernible in the proposed strip. Its curbside position supports a motor lane, but no specific turning movement is confirmed.

regions.model_reason: Retain the motor-lane classification. The satellite strip is car-width pavement extending to the actual curb, with sidewalk and landscaping outside it. No bicycle marking, parking stalls or parked vehicles are resolved within the strip. GSV supplies no spatially bound evidence requiring reclassification.
regions.model_binding: The curb return and landscaped sidewalk anchor the satellite region. A right-turn function is plausible, but the supplied views do not resolve an applicable arrow, ONLY marking, sign or sufficiently clear pocket transition. Curbside location alone does not establish dedicated permission.

initial_surface_audit.evidence: Continuous asphalt strip with longitudinal paint and several clearly visible vehicles. Vehicles obscure portions of the surface, but surrounding pavement supports a motor-vehicle lane rather than sidewalk or landscaping.

regions.model_reason: Retain the physical motor lane. Satellite vehicles occupy continuous roadway between longitudinal boundaries. The far-view crop resolves two marked motor-lane corridors on the centre side of the approach, consistent with r1 and r2 rather than parking or a buffer.
regions.model_binding: The farther-left bent pavement arrow belongs to the innermost of the two long-line-bounded corridors. Counting inward from the landscaped right kerb and three outer corridors provisionally binds this corridor to r1. The crop supports a left-turn-pocket interpretation, but no ONLY text is readable and queued vehicles interrupt tracing to the stopbar; dedicated use is a prediction, not confirmed legal permission.

initial_surface_audit.evidence: Road-colored pavement continues toward the stop-bar area between longitudinal markings. The approximately 3 m width supports a motor-vehicle lane; no convincing curb, planted buffer, parking treatment or bicycle marking is resolved within this strip. Faint pavement symbols are not readable.

regions.model_reason: Retain the motor lane. The satellite strip is asphalt between adjacent vehicle corridors. The far crop shows a second full-width arrow-bearing corridor, not a bicycle strip or painted buffer.
regions.model_binding: The nearer/right-hand left arrow lies in the outer member of the two left-side corridors, inside the three lanes extending toward the right kerb. This ordering provisionally binds it to r2. Its unbranched left arrow and pocket boundaries support predicted dedicated left use, although ONLY text is not readable and downstream continuity is partly obscured.

initial_surface_audit.evidence: A clearly visible dark vehicle occupies continuous asphalt between lane markings. Pavement and lane-line continuity extend toward the intersection. The vehicle and shadows obscure some markings.

regions.model_reason: Retain the motor lane. Satellite paint and an occupying dark vehicle establish roadway. In the mid view, a separate queued corridor lies between the two left-side corridors and the camera corridor.
regions.model_binding: Provisionally corresponds to the silver-hatchback corridor immediately left of the mid-view camera lane, with two further corridors toward the centre side. The satellite crop does not resolve a directional marking. Neither queue alignment nor position outside the left-turn pockets establishes through-only use.

initial_surface_audit.evidence: Car-width asphalt strip bounded by longitudinal lane paint and continuous with the approach pavement. No sidewalk texture, vegetation, parking stalls or readable bicycle marking is visible within the strip.

regions.model_reason: Retain the motor lane. Satellite pavement forms a full-width corridor inside the kerbside strip. Far and mid views show the corresponding penultimate motor corridor with lane separators.
regions.model_binding: Provisionally the far/mid camera corridor, one lane inward from the raised right kerb, occupied by the nearest white sedan in the mid view. The portable sign beside it is a temporary obstacle-passing/channelization graphic, not a bound permanent turn instruction. No readable pavement instruction establishes this lane's movements.

initial_surface_audit.evidence: The outer lane line and real kerb enclose a car-width paved strip, occupied by a vehicle near the stop bar. The light sidewalk and landscaping lie farther right. This supports a kerbside motor lane without requiring a readable turn arrow. The proposed lower-right flare is not wholly supported as roadway: portions approach or overlap the sidewalk/roadside structure and shadow, so pavement should not be extended to fill the polygon.

regions.model_reason: Retain the kerbside motor lane, excluding unsupported parts of the polygon flare. Satellite imagery shows a vehicle on asphalt beside the sidewalk. Far and mid views show car-width pavement outside the camera corridor extending to the raised kerb, without resolved bicycle markings, parking stalls or parked-car treatment. The lower-right polygon extends toward sidewalk and shadow and is not entirely lane pavement.
regions.model_binding: Correspondence follows the outer lane separator, landscaped sidewalk and rounded intersection corner. A right-turn role is plausible, but neither crop resolves an applicable permanent right-turn instruction. Temporary devices constrain the visible corridor without proving its closure or permanent use. Cross-street green surfacing is not an incoming bicycle strip.

initial_surface_audit.evidence: Continuous asphalt approach strip with longitudinal lane paint and a readable left-turn arrow. The strip reaches the intersection; overhead shadow obscures only part of it.

regions.model_reason: Retained. Satellite shows an asphalt pocket with a left-turn arrow, between the central separation and the incoming rail-bearing lane. The mid-view separator and rail ordering are consistent with this pocket.
regions.model_binding: The native crop binds a left-pointing arrow directly to r1. It does not resolve an applicable ONLY marking or conclusively exclude another arrow branch. Left-turn use is evidenced, but the complete movement set and dedicated status remain unresolved; the preliminary left_only prediction is withdrawn.

initial_surface_audit.evidence: Narrow longitudinal strip between the left-turn lane and the pale central track-like band. It may be part of a wider travel facility or its marginal separation; the image does not reliably establish an independent lane or a raised buffer.

regions.model_reason: Revised from the audit's unknown class. Joint evidence supports this narrow polygon as the left margin of a wider embedded-rail motor lane, rather than an independent lane or raised buffer.
regions.model_binding: r2-r4 jointly correspond to the paved rail-bearing lane between the left pocket and r5. The correspondence uses the track band and adjacent longitudinal divider, not vehicle heading. Neither crop establishes movement restrictions for this lane.

initial_surface_audit.evidence: A pale longitudinal band with parallel edges is visible. Its appearance is compatible with track infrastructure, but a raised separator cannot be excluded at this resolution. A vehicle overlaps its upper portion in projection, which alone does not resolve the surface beneath it.

regions.model_reason: Revised from unknown. The satellite pale band corresponds to embedded track pavement within the carriageway. Mid and far views support rails, rather than a raised separator, at this position.
regions.model_binding: The band lies between r1 and the divider bordering r5, matching the incoming track alignment. It is the central portion of the same physical lane as r2 and r4. Track continuation does not establish motor-vehicle permissions.
